correctness.rationale: The greedy shortest-prefix arch decomposition gives the universality index exactly: each arch is 0^r1 or 1^r0 (r>=1), followed by a unary remainder. Mark word length z, excess ones-minus-zeros x and arch count u. The exact Laurent rational generating function F=(1-z²)/(1+(1-2u)z²-z(1-uz²)(x+x^{-1})) follows, with balance equal to CT_x. Applying CT(1/(a-b(x+x^{-1})))=(a²-4b²)^(-1/2) and factoring yields B(t,u)=sqrt((1-t)/(1-(1+4u)t+4u²t²)). Dominant root rho(u)=2/(1+4u+sqrt(1+8u)) is analytic around u=1 and provides mean 2n/3+2/9+O(1/n), variance 4n/27-2/81+O(1/n), and a Gaussian CLT by local quasi-powers/characteristic functions. Independent exhaustive enumeration of balanced words at each n=1,...,7 agreed with coefficients and both high-index boundary counts. Enumeration does not establish the all-n formula or CLT; the formal constant term and analytic transfer do.

originality.rationale: The prior 2026 published binary universality law has rational GF (1+z)/(1-z-2uz²), summing over ALL binary words of each length, and is not the fixed-composition specialization. The submitted radical counts only exactly n zeros and n ones, adds conditional asymptotics. Day et al. study fixed-length scattered-factor spectra and maximum-universality boundary; arch factorization itself is old. No inspected earlier statement encodes the precise conditional radical law. An earlier Dyck-word enumeration has an algebraic transform relation but applies to nonnegative-prefix paths, not arbitrary bridges; possible implicit coverage through transform identities remains a risk.
